PFQ

Physical Fitness Qualification

POLICE FITNESS TEST

At a glance

The National Tactical Officers Association (NTOA) has a five-part fitness test that mixes running and bodyweight exercises. It is more than one run, and each part contributes to the final score.

FEATURED ACTIVITY800 m run3:14 or faster earns 10 points

What the test includes

  • 800 m run
  • 400 m run carrying weights
  • Burpees for 3 minutes
  • Squats for 2 minutes
  • Strict pull-ups for 1 minute

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

Five consecutive events, with three minutes between efforts and a judge for each participant. This is a proposed SWAT fitness benchmark, not a universal hiring standard.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

Scoring and scope

Base event scores are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10. At least 30 total and no zero-score event are required. For each run, a full 15 seconds below the top threshold adds one point. Each additional valid repetition beyond the top repetition target adds one point. The challenge ranking and the minimum qualification are distinct; use the official judge’s scorecard.

  • Full PFQ scoring instructions

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Build comfortable continuous running and a separate interval session; use repeatable 400 m efforts before combining events.
  • Train carries, squat endurance and strict pulling in separate blocks. Introduce event duration and load only once movement remains controlled.
  • Rehearse event order and three-minute recovery at submaximal effort; log valid repetitions rather than total attempts.

Putting it into a training week

Use separate running and strength sessions first. Only combine the five events once you can complete each with controlled technique; do not practise mask-based exertion independently.

Common mistakes

  • Treating a fast first run as a substitute for balanced capacity across all five events.
  • Using partial repetitions or unfamiliar load. Do not improvise restricted-breathing or mask drills for home practice.

What to log

Record both run times, valid repetitions for each timed event, load, rest intervals and any invalid movements.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

  • The organisation describes this as a proposed fitness standard, not a universal requirement for every police department.
